name: deployment
//pinning: Every version below is EXACT — no ^ ranges. A caret on aws-cdk-lib means two
installs a week apart synthesize different CloudFormation from the same commit,
and for a sample that people deploy into their own accounts that is a
supply-chain and a reproducibility problem at once. Upgrading is now a visible,
reviewable diff. The versions are the ones this tree was last built and
pnpm-lock.yaml is the ONE lockfile. package-lock.json used to sit beside it and
the two had already drifted (package-lock said aws-cdk-lib 2.258.1 while
node_modules held 2.266.0), which is the whole problem with keeping both: the
one you install from is whichever tool you happened to run. It was deleted, and
`packageManager` below plus an `npm` preinstall guard keep it from coming back.
Install with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` (or `make cdk-install`), never a
bare `install` — frozen fails on a lockfile that disagrees with this file
instead of quietly resolving past it.

scripts.preinstall:
node -e "if(!(process.env.npm_config_user_agent||'').startsWith('pnpm')){console.error('
Use pnpm, not npm: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm-lock.yaml is the only lockfile here; npm would write a second one.
');process.exit(1)}"
